name: Burg Tratzberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Tratzberg near Jenbach delights visitors as an impeccably preserved Renaissance jewel perched high above the Inn Valley with lavish state rooms.
preis: Castle tour adults approx. €14.50; Tratzberg-Express train extra
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from early April to early November from 10:00 to 16:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The magnificent Schloss Tratzberg stands majestically upon a wooded ridge high above the Inn Valley between Jenbach and Stans. Recognised as one of Europe's finest and most authentically preserved Renaissance castles, Tratzberg offers an extraordinary window into 16th-century aristocratic life. Originally built as a border bastion against Bavaria and lavishly reconstructed around 1500 by wealthy silver-mining tycoons from Schwaz, the castle was further enhanced by the famous Fugger merchant dynasty and later the Counts of Enzenberg into a masterpiece of late Gothic and Renaissance living culture. Its completely furnished state rooms, elaborate wooden coffered ceilings, celebrated Habsburg genealogy fresco, and arcaded inner courtyard bring history vividly to life.

Route & Requirements

Visiting Schloss Tratzberg is an enchanting cultural highlight for adults, historians, and families alike. From the valley car park near the Schlosswirt inn, visitors can enjoy a scenic 20-minute walk through peaceful beech woodland or board the cheerful Tratzberg Express shuttle train. The interior tour features state-of-the-art radio dramatisation audio guides voiced by historical characters. Children enjoy a dedicated fairytale audio tour accompanied by a treasure hunt. The castle interior tour lasts roughly one hour; comfortable shoes are recommended for the forest path.

Visiting & Getting There

Schloss Tratzberg enjoys prime accessibility in the lower Inn Valley near Jenbach. Jenbach railway station is a major stop on the international rail network served by Railjet and regional S-Bahn lines, with quick bus and taxi connections to the castle base. Drivers take the A12 Inntal motorway exiting at Schwaz or Jenbach. Ample parking is available at the valley base. The castle is open daily from late March through early November. Advance tickets can be purchased online or at the ticket counter.

Tips

Do not miss the monumental 46-metre-long Habsburg genealogical mural in the Great Hall, displaying 148 lifelike portraits including Emperor Maximilian I. Following the tour, relax in the sunny beer garden of the Schlosswirt inn at the foot of the hill, enjoying authentic Tyrolean delicacies while children explore the adventure playground. Combine your excursion with a nostalgic ride on the Jenbach steam cog railway up to Lake Achensee.
